newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegro bourse Feb turnover plunges further.
newsitem.headline: Montenegro bourse Feb turnover plunges further.

text.p: The Montenegro Stock Exchange said on Friday its February turnover plunged 38.45 percent and traders cited banks' insolvency and a change of the reserve requirement as the key reason for the fall.
Total February turnover dropped to 21.35 million dinars ($3.76 million) in 87 transactions, from 34.69 million dinars in 121 deals in Janaury, the bourse said.

"Besides poor liquidity of the banking sector, the change in the central bank's reserve requirement regulation had a strong negative impact on the bourse turnover," Natasa Bulajic of the bourse told Reuters.
The new reserve requirement regulations oblige banks to deposit with the central bank 15 percent of money lent to other banks in the period from February 28 to June 30.
Banks currently transfer 15 percent of their deposits to fulfill the central bank's reserve requirement.

"The change in regulation obviously additionally drained already tight market liquidity boosting companies' and banks' demands for cash," Bulajic said. "But like in January, there was and still is no money on offer."
In January, the bourse reported a sharp 24.95 percent decline over December, blaming tight liquidity of the banking sector for the plunge.
In February, the bourse traded only in companies' short-term securities which accounted for 11.527 million dinars or 53.98 percent of the total.
Short-term bonds accounted for 9.6 million dinars or 83.43 percent, while the segment of commercial papers was 1.9 million or 16.57 percent.
The giro-money market segment, where banks trade their surplus liquidity, accounted for remaining 9.827 million dinars of February turnover, the bourse said.
Interest rates on short term securites stabilised at an annual 297.03 percent, with maturity most frequently standing at 10-15 days.
The bourse reported no trade in the central bank short-term bonds.
"The National Bank of Yugoslavia has not auctioned its bonds on the Podgorica-based bourse since last August," Bulajic said.
